ELUCIDATION
ON
REGIONAL REGULATION
NUMBER YEAR
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL
Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The State holds the view that all forms of violence, especially domestic violence, constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as forms of discrimination.

The State's view is based on Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, along with its amendments. Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under his/her control, and shall have the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not do something which is a basic right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to obtain facilities and special treatment to obtain the same opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice".

Current developments show that acts of physical, psychological, sexual violence, and domestic neglect in reality occur so that adequate legal instruments are needed to eliminate violence, especially domestic violence. Legal reform that sides with vulnerable or subordinated groups, especially women and children, becomes very necessary in connection with the many cases of violence, especially domestic violence, this also occurs in South Tangerang City, in 2010 violence cases reported to the Tangerang Police totaled 143 cases, at the South Jakarta Metro Police 56 cases were recorded, Tigaraksa Police - 19 - Tangerang Regency 23 cases and in 2011 70 cases were recorded at the South Jakarta Metro Police and 28 cases at the Tigaraksa Police Tangerang Regency, this does not yet reflect the actual conditions in society, because cases of violence especially those occurring within the household are still considered disgraceful in the view of society and also the courage of the community to report incidents still needs to be increased, therefore a regional regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence needs to be possessed by South Tangerang City.

The emergence of cases of violence against children and women is often caused by factors that develop in society, for example low economic levels, education, social environment and others. Therefore, victims of such violence need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights. From the above framework, the Regional Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to suppress, prevent, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against children and women.

In conducting guidance, development and protection of women and children, the role of society is needed, whether through women and children protection institutions, religious institutions, non-governmental organizations, community organizations, social organizations, business world, mass media, or educational institutions.

This Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children from violence is closely related to several other laws and regulations already in force, among others, Law Number 1 of 1946 concerning the Criminal Code and its Amendments, Law Number 8 of 1981 concerning the Criminal Procedure Code, Law Number 1 of 1974 concerning Marriage, Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human - 20 - Rights and most importantly Law number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence and Law number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

This Regional Regulation, in addition to regulating matters of prevention and protection as well as recovery for victims of violence, also regulates matters of obligations for law enforcement officers, health workers, social workers, volunteer companions, or spiritual counselors to protect victims so that they are more sensitive and responsive. To carry out violence prevention, Agencies or Offices that have duties and responsibilities related to the field of women's empowerment and child protection implement preventive actions, among others, organizing communication, information, and education about violence prevention, protection of women and children.

Based on these considerations, it is time to establish a Regional Regulation in South Tangerang City concerning the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, especially Domestic Violence, which is regulated comprehensively, clearly, and firmly to protect and side with victims, as well as simultaneously provide education and awareness to the community and officials that all acts of violence constitute crimes against human dignity.

CHAPTER VII
FORMS OF VIOLENCE AND PROTECTION
Article 11
(1) Forms of violence against Women and Children include physical, sexual, economic and psychological.
(2) Forms of physical violence are any acts that result in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and or cause death.
- 14 - (3) Forms of sexual violence are sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or specific purposes.
(4) Forms of economic violence are neglect of family members in the form of not providing a proper living, care or maintenance.
(5) Forms of psychological violence are acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering in a person.

Article 17
Paragraph (1) What is meant by administrative sanctions is that the institution or body that implements protection services for women and children is no longer established and or recognized by the Regional Government.
Paragraph (2) Criminal sanctions for perpetrators of violence are regulated by Law number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence article 44 through article 50; Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection Article 77 through article 90, and Law Number 1 of 1946 concerning the Criminal Code and its Amendments, Law Number 8 of 1981 concerning the Criminal Procedure Code Paragraph (3) Sufficiently clear.

VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE.
CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this regional regulation, what is meant by:
1. Regional Government is the Mayor, and regional apparatus as elements of the organizer of the Regional Government of South Tangerang City.
- 8 -
2. Mayor is the Mayor of South Tangerang.
3. Implementation is the form of execution of protection for women and children victims of violence.
4. Woman is a person who has female genitalia, can experience menstruation, pregnancy, childbirth, breastfeeding and includes a person who has obtained legal status as a Woman.
5. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including those in the womb.
6. Violence is any act that results in or can result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim.
7. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
8. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death.
9. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.
10. Economic violence is any act that neglects family members in the form of not providing a proper living, care or maintenance.
11. Psychological violence is any act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person.
12. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
- 9 -
13. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutor's office, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
14. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
15. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter referred to as P2TP2A is an institution that provides services and protection for women and children especially those who have problems due to acts of violence, discrimination, human trafficking and other social problems in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psycho-social, public facility services and legal protection and assistance.
16. Community Social Institution is a Non-Governmental Organization (NGO) and or other Community Organizations.
17. Population is Citizens of South Tangerang and foreigners who enter legally and reside in the area of South Tangerang City.
18. Service is an action that must be immediately taken to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
19. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy in order to provide strengthening and recovery for victims of violence as determined in a decision of an authorized official.
20. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy and spiritual guidance for the self-strengthening of victims of violence especially victims of domestic violence to resolve the problems they face.
- 10 -
21. Integrated Service Center hereinafter referred to as PPT is a unified unit that carries out integrated service functions for women and children victims of violence, based in hospitals, Community Health Centers, P2TP2A and other similar institutions that are managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psycho-social and legal services.

Article 5
Letter a What is meant by health services are efforts that include promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects.
Letter b What is meant by receiving psychological assistance is assistance provided by a psychologist to victims who suffer from trauma/other mental problems to restore the victim's mental condition. Meanwhile, legal assistance is an aid effort provided by a person and/legal aid institution to the victim at every level of examination and throughout the legal process.
Letter c What is meant by counseling is the provision of assistance by an expert or a person who is trained in such a way that the victim's psychological understanding and ability increases in solving the problems faced.
Letter d what is meant by spiritual guidance is counseling provided by a clergyman.
Letter e What is meant by resocialization is that the victim can live life again in society including in the restoration of their good name.
Letter f What is meant by empowerment is Empowerment means making something become empowered or have power or have strength.
- 23 -

Article 3
The Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence aims to provide prevention, protection, and services to women and children against gender-based violence and the best interests of children that occur in households or public.

Article 13
(1) Forms of protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence consist of medical, legal, medicolegal (forensic medicine), economic and psychological protection.
(2) The form of medical protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence as referred to in paragraph (1), consists of treatment and recovery of physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of victims carried out by medical personnel and paramedics.
- 15 - (3) The form of legal protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence as referred to in paragraph (1), consists of services and assistance to help victims undergo legal and judicial processes.
(4) The form of medicolegal protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence as referred to in paragraph (1), consists of medical services for the purpose of evidence in the legal field.
(5) The form of psychological protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence as referred to in paragraph (1), consists of assistance in order to restore the traumatic condition of victims including provision of safe houses to protect victims from various threats and intimidation for victims and providing psychological support so that victims have self-confidence, strength and independence in resolving problems.
(6) The form of economic protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence as referred to in paragraph (1), consists of services for skills and providing economic access so that victims can be independent.

Article 12
(1) Every woman and child who becomes a victim of violence must receive protection in accordance with applicable provisions.
(2) Protection of women and children victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be provided to residents of South Tangerang City whether it occurs in South Tangerang City or outside South Tangerang City.
(3) Protection of women and children victims of violence as an initial action shall also be provided to non-residents of South Tangerang City where the incident occurs within the territory of South Tangerang City, followed by coordination with the region of origin of said residents.

SOURCES OF FUNDS AND REPORTING
Article 16

I. GENERAL
Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The State holds the view that all forms of violence, especially domestic violence, constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as forms of discrimination.

The State's view is based on Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, along with its amendments. Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under his/her control, and shall have the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not do something which is a basic right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to obtain facilities and special treatment to obtain the same opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice".

Current developments show that acts of physical, psychological, sexual violence, and domestic neglect in reality occur so that adequate legal instruments are needed to eliminate violence, especially domestic violence. Legal reform that sides with vulnerable or subordinated groups, especially women and children, becomes very necessary in connection with the many cases of violence, especially domestic violence, this also occurs in South Tangerang City, in 2010 violence cases reported to the Tangerang Police totaled 143 cases, at the South Jakarta Metro Police 56 cases were recorded, Tigaraksa Police - 19 - Tangerang Regency 23 cases and in 2011 70 cases were recorded at the South Jakarta Metro Police and 28 cases at the Tigaraksa Police Tangerang Regency, this does not yet reflect the actual conditions in society, because cases of violence especially those occurring within the household are still considered disgraceful in the view of society and also the courage of the community to report incidents still needs to be increased, therefore a regional regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence needs to be possessed by South Tangerang City.

The emergence of cases of violence against children and women is often caused by factors that develop in society, for example low economic levels, education, social environment and others. Therefore, victims of such violence need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights. From the above framework, the Regional Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to suppress, prevent, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against children and women.

In conducting guidance, development and protection of women and children, the role of society is needed, whether through women and children protection institutions, religious institutions, non-governmental organizations, community organizations, social organizations, business world, mass media, or educational institutions.

This Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children from violence is closely related to several other laws and regulations already in force, among others, Law Number 1 of 1946 concerning the Criminal Code and its Amendments, Law Number 8 of 1981 concerning the Criminal Procedure Code, Law Number 1 of 1974 concerning Marriage, Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human - 20 - Rights and most importantly Law number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence and Law number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

This Regional Regulation, in addition to regulating matters of prevention and protection as well as recovery for victims of violence, also regulates matters of obligations for law enforcement officers, health workers, social workers, volunteer companions, or spiritual counselors to protect victims so that they are more sensitive and responsive. To carry out violence prevention, Agencies or Offices that have duties and responsibilities related to the field of women's empowerment and child protection implement preventive actions, among others, organizing communication, information, and education about violence prevention, protection of women and children.

Based on these considerations, it is time to establish a Regional Regulation in South Tangerang City concerning the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, especially Domestic Violence, which is regulated comprehensively, clearly, and firmly to protect and side with victims, as well as simultaneously provide education and awareness to the community and officials that all acts of violence constitute crimes against human dignity.

Article 1

ON

NUMBER YEAR

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL
Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The State holds the view that all forms of violence, especially domestic violence, constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as forms of discrimination.

The State's view is based on Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, along with its amendments. Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under his/her control, and shall have the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not do something which is a basic right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to obtain facilities and special treatment to obtain the same opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice".

Current developments show that acts of physical, psychological, sexual violence, and domestic neglect in reality occur so that adequate legal instruments are needed to eliminate violence, especially domestic violence. Legal reform that sides with vulnerable or subordinated groups, especially women and children, becomes very necessary in connection with the many cases of violence, especially domestic violence, this also occurs in South Tangerang City, in 2010 violence cases reported to the Tangerang Police totaled 143 cases, at the South Jakarta Metro Police 56 cases were recorded, Tigaraksa Police - 19 - Tangerang Regency 23 cases and in 2011 70 cases were recorded at the South Jakarta Metro Police and 28 cases at the Tigaraksa Police Tangerang Regency, this does not yet reflect the actual conditions in society, because cases of violence especially those occurring within the household are still considered disgraceful in the view of society and also the courage of the community to report incidents still needs to be increased, therefore a regional regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence needs to be possessed by South Tangerang City.

The emergence of cases of violence against children and women is often caused by factors that develop in society, for example low economic levels, education, social environment and others. Therefore, victims of such violence need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights. From the above framework, the Regional Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to suppress, prevent, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against children and women.

In conducting guidance, development and protection of women and children, the role of society is needed, whether through women and children protection institutions, religious institutions, non-governmental organizations, community organizations, social organizations, business world, mass media, or educational institutions.

This Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children from violence is closely related to several other laws and regulations already in force, among others, Law Number 1 of 1946 concerning the Criminal Code and its Amendments, Law Number 8 of 1981 concerning the Criminal Procedure Code, Law Number 1 of 1974 concerning Marriage, Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human - 20 - Rights and most importantly Law number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence and Law number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

This Regional Regulation, in addition to regulating matters of prevention and protection as well as recovery for victims of violence, also regulates matters of obligations for law enforcement officers, health workers, social workers, volunteer companions, or spiritual counselors to protect victims so that they are more sensitive and responsive. To carry out violence prevention, Agencies or Offices that have duties and responsibilities related to the field of women's empowerment and child protection implement preventive actions, among others, organizing communication, information, and education about violence prevention, protection of women and children.

Based on these considerations, it is time to establish a Regional Regulation in South Tangerang City concerning the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, especially Domestic Violence, which is regulated comprehensively, clearly, and firmly to protect and side with victims, as well as simultaneously provide education and awareness to the community and officials that all acts of violence constitute crimes against human dignity.

I. GENERAL
Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The State holds the view that all forms of violence, especially domestic violence, constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as forms of discrimination.

The State's view is based on Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, along with its amendments. Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under his/her control, and shall have the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not do something which is a basic right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to obtain facilities and special treatment to obtain the same opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice".

Current developments show that acts of physical, psychological, sexual violence, and domestic neglect in reality occur so that adequate legal instruments are needed to eliminate violence, especially domestic violence. Legal reform that sides with vulnerable or subordinated groups, especially women and children, becomes very necessary in connection with the many cases of violence, especially domestic violence, this also occurs in South Tangerang City, in 2010 violence cases reported to the Tangerang Police totaled 143 cases, at the South Jakarta Metro Police 56 cases were recorded, Tigaraksa Police - 19 - Tangerang Regency 23 cases and in 2011 70 cases were recorded at the South Jakarta Metro Police and 28 cases at the Tigaraksa Police Tangerang Regency, this does not yet reflect the actual conditions in society, because cases of violence especially those occurring within the household are still considered disgraceful in the view of society and also the courage of the community to report incidents still needs to be increased, therefore a regional regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence needs to be possessed by South Tangerang City.

The emergence of cases of violence against children and women is often caused by factors that develop in society, for example low economic levels, education, social environment and others. Therefore, victims of such violence need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights. From the above framework, the Regional Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to suppress, prevent, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against children and women.

In conducting guidance, development and protection of women and children, the role of society is needed, whether through women and children protection institutions, religious institutions, non-governmental organizations, community organizations, social organizations, business world, mass media, or educational institutions.

This Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children from violence is closely related to several other laws and regulations already in force, among others, Law Number 1 of 1946 concerning the Criminal Code and its Amendments, Law Number 8 of 1981 concerning the Criminal Procedure Code, Law Number 1 of 1974 concerning Marriage, Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human - 20 - Rights and most importantly Law number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence and Law number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

This Regional Regulation, in addition to regulating matters of prevention and protection as well as recovery for victims of violence, also regulates matters of obligations for law enforcement officers, health workers, social workers, volunteer companions, or spiritual counselors to protect victims so that they are more sensitive and responsive. To carry out violence prevention, Agencies or Offices that have duties and responsibilities related to the field of women's empowerment and child protection implement preventive actions, among others, organizing communication, information, and education about violence prevention, protection of women and children.

Based on these considerations, it is time to establish a Regional Regulation in South Tangerang City concerning the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, especially Domestic Violence, which is regulated comprehensively, clearly, and firmly to protect and side with victims, as well as simultaneously provide education and awareness to the community and officials that all acts of violence constitute crimes against human dignity.

I. GENERAL
Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The State holds the view that all forms of violence, especially domestic violence, constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as forms of discrimination.

The State's view is based on Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, along with its amendments. Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under his/her control, and shall have the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not do something which is a basic right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to obtain facilities and special treatment to obtain the same opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice".

Current developments show that acts of physical, psychological, sexual violence, and domestic neglect in reality occur so that adequate legal instruments are needed to eliminate violence, especially domestic violence. Legal reform that sides with vulnerable or subordinated groups, especially women and children, becomes very necessary in connection with the many cases of violence, especially domestic violence, this also occurs in South Tangerang City, in 2010 violence cases reported to the Tangerang Police totaled 143 cases, at the South Jakarta Metro Police 56 cases were recorded, Tigaraksa Police - 19 - Tangerang Regency 23 cases and in 2011 70 cases were recorded at the South Jakarta Metro Police and 28 cases at the Tigaraksa Police Tangerang Regency, this does not yet reflect the actual conditions in society, because cases of violence especially those occurring within the household are still considered disgraceful in the view of society and also the courage of the community to report incidents still needs to be increased, therefore a regional regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence needs to be possessed by South Tangerang City.

The emergence of cases of violence against children and women is often caused by factors that develop in society, for example low economic levels, education, social environment and others. Therefore, victims of such violence need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights. From the above framework, the Regional Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to suppress, prevent, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against children and women.

In conducting guidance, development and protection of women and children, the role of society is needed, whether through women and children protection institutions, religious institutions, non-governmental organizations, community organizations, social organizations, business world, mass media, or educational institutions.

This Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children from violence is closely related to several other laws and regulations already in force, among others, Law Number 1 of 1946 concerning the Criminal Code and its Amendments, Law Number 8 of 1981 concerning the Criminal Procedure Code, Law Number 1 of 1974 concerning Marriage, Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human - 20 - Rights and most importantly Law number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence and Law number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

This Regional Regulation, in addition to regulating matters of prevention and protection as well as recovery for victims of violence, also regulates matters of obligations for law enforcement officers, health workers, social workers, volunteer companions, or spiritual counselors to protect victims so that they are more sensitive and responsive. To carry out violence prevention, Agencies or Offices that have duties and responsibilities related to the field of women's empowerment and child protection implement preventive actions, among others, organizing communication, information, and education about violence prevention, protection of women and children.

Based on these considerations, it is time to establish a Regional Regulation in South Tangerang City concerning the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, especially Domestic Violence, which is regulated comprehensively, clearly, and firmly to protect and side with victims, as well as simultaneously provide education and awareness to the community and officials that all acts of violence constitute crimes against human dignity.

I. GENERAL
Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The State holds the view that all forms of violence, especially domestic violence, constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as forms of discrimination.

The State's view is based on Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, along with its amendments. Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under his/her control, and shall have the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not do something which is a basic right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to obtain facilities and special treatment to obtain the same opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice".

Current developments show that acts of physical, psychological, sexual violence, and domestic neglect in reality occur so that adequate legal instruments are needed to eliminate violence, especially domestic violence. Legal reform that sides with vulnerable or subordinated groups, especially women and children, becomes very necessary in connection with the many cases of violence, especially domestic violence, this also occurs in South Tangerang City, in 2010 violence cases reported to the Tangerang Police totaled 143 cases, at the South Jakarta Metro Police 56 cases were recorded, Tigaraksa Police - 19 - Tangerang Regency 23 cases and in 2011 70 cases were recorded at the South Jakarta Metro Police and 28 cases at the Tigaraksa Police Tangerang Regency, this does not yet reflect the actual conditions in society, because cases of violence especially those occurring within the household are still considered disgraceful in the view of society and also the courage of the community to report incidents still needs to be increased, therefore a regional regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence needs to be possessed by South Tangerang City.

The emergence of cases of violence against children and women is often caused by factors that develop in society, for example low economic levels, education, social environment and others. Therefore, victims of such violence need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights. From the above framework, the Regional Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to suppress, prevent, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against children and women.

In conducting guidance, development and protection of women and children, the role of society is needed, whether through women and children protection institutions, religious institutions, non-governmental organizations, community organizations, social organizations, business world, mass media, or educational institutions.

This Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children from violence is closely related to several other laws and regulations already in force, among others, Law Number 1 of 1946 concerning the Criminal Code and its Amendments, Law Number 8 of 1981 concerning the Criminal Procedure Code, Law Number 1 of 1974 concerning Marriage, Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human - 20 - Rights and most importantly Law number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence and Law number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

This Regional Regulation, in addition to regulating matters of prevention and protection as well as recovery for victims of violence, also regulates matters of obligations for law enforcement officers, health workers, social workers, volunteer companions, or spiritual counselors to protect victims so that they are more sensitive and responsive. To carry out violence prevention, Agencies or Offices that have duties and responsibilities related to the field of women's empowerment and child protection implement preventive actions, among others, organizing communication, information, and education about violence prevention, protection of women and children.

Based on these considerations, it is time to establish a Regional Regulation in South Tangerang City concerning the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, especially Domestic Violence, which is regulated comprehensively, clearly, and firmly to protect and side with victims, as well as simultaneously provide education and awareness to the community and officials that all acts of violence constitute crimes against human dignity.

ELUCIDATION
ON
REGIONAL REGULATION
NUMBER YEAR
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL
Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The State holds the view that all forms of violence, especially domestic violence, constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as forms of discrimination.

The State's view is based on Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, along with its amendments. Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under his/her control, and shall have the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not do something which is a basic right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to obtain facilities and special treatment to obtain the same opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice".

Current developments show that acts of physical, psychological, sexual violence, and domestic neglect in reality occur so that adequate legal instruments are needed to eliminate violence, especially domestic violence. Legal reform that sides with vulnerable or subordinated groups, especially women and children, becomes very necessary in connection with the many cases of violence, especially domestic violence, this also occurs in South Tangerang City, in 2010 violence cases reported to the Tangerang Police totaled 143 cases, at the South Jakarta Metro Police 56 cases were recorded, Tigaraksa Police - 19 - Tangerang Regency 23 cases and in 2011 70 cases were recorded at the South Jakarta Metro Police and 28 cases at the Tigaraksa Police Tangerang Regency, this does not yet reflect the actual conditions in society, because cases of violence especially those occurring within the household are still considered disgraceful in the view of society and also the courage of the community to report incidents still needs to be increased, therefore a regional regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence needs to be possessed by South Tangerang City.

The emergence of cases of violence against children and women is often caused by factors that develop in society, for example low economic levels, education, social environment and others. Therefore, victims of such violence need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights. From the above framework, the Regional Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to suppress, prevent, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against children and women.

In conducting guidance, development and protection of women and children, the role of society is needed, whether through women and children protection institutions, religious institutions, non-governmental organizations, community organizations, social organizations, business world, mass media, or educational institutions.

This Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children from violence is closely related to several other laws and regulations already in force, among others, Law Number 1 of 1946 concerning the Criminal Code and its Amendments, Law Number 8 of 1981 concerning the Criminal Procedure Code, Law Number 1 of 1974 concerning Marriage, Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human - 20 - Rights and most importantly Law number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence and Law number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

This Regional Regulation, in addition to regulating matters of prevention and protection as well as recovery for victims of violence, also regulates matters of obligations for law enforcement officers, health workers, social workers, volunteer companions, or spiritual counselors to protect victims so that they are more sensitive and responsive. To carry out violence prevention, Agencies or Offices that have duties and responsibilities related to the field of women's empowerment and child protection implement preventive actions, among others, organizing communication, information, and education about violence prevention, protection of women and children.

Based on these considerations, it is time to establish a Regional Regulation in South Tangerang City concerning the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, especially Domestic Violence, which is regulated comprehensively, clearly, and firmly to protect and side with victims, as well as simultaneously provide education and awareness to the community and officials that all acts of violence constitute crimes against human dignity.

I. GENERAL
Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The State holds the view that all forms of violence, especially domestic violence, constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as forms of discrimination.

The State's view is based on Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, along with its amendments. Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under his/her control, and shall have the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not do something which is a basic right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to obtain facilities and special treatment to obtain the same opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice".

Current developments show that acts of physical, psychological, sexual violence, and domestic neglect in reality occur so that adequate legal instruments are needed to eliminate violence, especially domestic violence. Legal reform that sides with vulnerable or subordinated groups, especially women and children, becomes very necessary in connection with the many cases of violence, especially domestic violence, this also occurs in South Tangerang City, in 2010 violence cases reported to the Tangerang Police totaled 143 cases, at the South Jakarta Metro Police 56 cases were recorded, Tigaraksa Police - 19 - Tangerang Regency 23 cases and in 2011 70 cases were recorded at the South Jakarta Metro Police and 28 cases at the Tigaraksa Police Tangerang Regency, this does not yet reflect the actual conditions in society, because cases of violence especially those occurring within the household are still considered disgraceful in the view of society and also the courage of the community to report incidents still needs to be increased, therefore a regional regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence needs to be possessed by South Tangerang City.

The emergence of cases of violence against children and women is often caused by factors that develop in society, for example low economic levels, education, social environment and others. Therefore, victims of such violence need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights. From the above framework, the Regional Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to suppress, prevent, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against children and women.

In conducting guidance, development and protection of women and children, the role of society is needed, whether through women and children protection institutions, religious institutions, non-governmental organizations, community organizations, social organizations, business world, mass media, or educational institutions.

This Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children from violence is closely related to several other laws and regulations already in force, among others, Law Number 1 of 1946 concerning the Criminal Code and its Amendments, Law Number 8 of 1981 concerning the Criminal Procedure Code, Law Number 1 of 1974 concerning Marriage, Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human - 20 - Rights and most importantly Law number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence and Law number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

This Regional Regulation, in addition to regulating matters of prevention and protection as well as recovery for victims of violence, also regulates matters of obligations for law enforcement officers, health workers, social workers, volunteer companions, or spiritual counselors to protect victims so that they are more sensitive and responsive. To carry out violence prevention, Agencies or Offices that have duties and responsibilities related to the field of women's empowerment and child protection implement preventive actions, among others, organizing communication, information, and education about violence prevention, protection of women and children.

Based on these considerations, it is time to establish a Regional Regulation in South Tangerang City concerning the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, especially Domestic Violence, which is regulated comprehensively, clearly, and firmly to protect and side with victims, as well as simultaneously provide education and awareness to the community and officials that all acts of violence constitute crimes against human dignity.

ELUCIDATION
ON
REGIONAL REGULATION
NUMBER YEAR
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL
Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The State holds the view that all forms of violence, especially domestic violence, constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as forms of discrimination.

The State's view is based on Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, along with its amendments. Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under his/her control, and shall have the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not do something which is a basic right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to obtain facilities and special treatment to obtain the same opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice".

Current developments show that acts of physical, psychological, sexual violence, and domestic neglect in reality occur so that adequate legal instruments are needed to eliminate violence, especially domestic violence. Legal reform that sides with vulnerable or subordinated groups, especially women and children, becomes very necessary in connection with the many cases of violence, especially domestic violence, this also occurs in South Tangerang City, in 2010 violence cases reported to the Tangerang Police totaled 143 cases, at the South Jakarta Metro Police 56 cases were recorded, Tigaraksa Police - 19 - Tangerang Regency 23 cases and in 2011 70 cases were recorded at the South Jakarta Metro Police and 28 cases at the Tigaraksa Police Tangerang Regency, this does not yet reflect the actual conditions in society, because cases of violence especially those occurring within the household are still considered disgraceful in the view of society and also the courage of the community to report incidents still needs to be increased, therefore a regional regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence needs to be possessed by South Tangerang City.

The emergence of cases of violence against children and women is often caused by factors that develop in society, for example low economic levels, education, social environment and others. Therefore, victims of such violence need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights. From the above framework, the Regional Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to suppress, prevent, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against children and women.

In conducting guidance, development and protection of women and children, the role of society is needed, whether through women and children protection institutions, religious institutions, non-governmental organizations, community organizations, social organizations, business world, mass media, or educational institutions.

This Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children from violence is closely related to several other laws and regulations already in force, among others, Law Number 1 of 1946 concerning the Criminal Code and its Amendments, Law Number 8 of 1981 concerning the Criminal Procedure Code, Law Number 1 of 1974 concerning Marriage, Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human - 20 - Rights and most importantly Law number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence and Law number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

This Regional Regulation, in addition to regulating matters of prevention and protection as well as recovery for victims of violence, also regulates matters of obligations for law enforcement officers, health workers, social workers, volunteer companions, or spiritual counselors to protect victims so that they are more sensitive and responsive. To carry out violence prevention, Agencies or Offices that have duties and responsibilities related to the field of women's empowerment and child protection implement preventive actions, among others, organizing communication, information, and education about violence prevention, protection of women and children.

Based on these considerations, it is time to establish a Regional Regulation in South Tangerang City concerning the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, especially Domestic Violence, which is regulated comprehensively, clearly, and firmly to protect and side with victims, as well as simultaneously provide education and awareness to the community and officials that all acts of violence constitute crimes against human dignity.

Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The State holds the view that all forms of violence, especially domestic violence, constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as forms of discrimination.

The State's view is based on Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, along with its amendments. Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to obtain facilities and special treatment to obtain the same opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice".

Current developments show that acts of physical, psychological, sexual violence, and domestic neglect in reality occur so that adequate legal instruments are needed to eliminate violence, especially domestic violence. Legal reform that sides with vulnerable or subordinated groups, especially women and children, becomes very necessary in connection with the many cases of violence, especially domestic violence, this also occurs in South Tangerang City, in 2010 violence cases reported to the Tangerang Police totaled 143 cases, at the South Jakarta Metro Police 56 cases were recorded, Tigaraksa Police - 19 - Tangerang Regency 23 cases and in 2011 70 cases were recorded at the South Jakarta Metro Police and 28 cases at the Tigaraksa Police Tangerang Regency, this does not yet reflect the actual conditions in society, because cases of violence especially those occurring within the household are still considered disgraceful in the view of society and also the courage of the community to report incidents still needs to be increased, therefore a regional regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence needs to be possessed by South Tangerang City.

Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The State holds the view that all forms of violence, especially domestic violence, constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as forms of discrimination.

The State's view is based on Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, along with its amendments. Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under his/her control, and shall have the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not do something which is a basic right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to obtain facilities and special treatment to obtain the same opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice".

Current developments show that acts of physical, psychological, sexual violence, and domestic neglect in reality occur so that adequate legal instruments are needed to eliminate violence, especially domestic violence. Legal reform that sides with vulnerable or subordinated groups, especially women and children, becomes very necessary in connection with the many cases of violence, especially domestic violence, this also occurs in South Tangerang City, in 2010 violence cases reported to the Tangerang Police totaled 143 cases, at the South Jakarta Metro Police 56 cases were recorded, Tigaraksa Police - 19 - Tangerang Regency 23 cases and in 2011 70 cases were recorded at the South Jakarta Metro Police and 28 cases at the Tigaraksa Police Tangerang Regency, this does not yet reflect the actual conditions in society, because cases of violence especially those occurring within the household are still considered disgraceful in the view of society and also the courage of the community to report incidents still needs to be increased, therefore a regional regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence needs to be possessed by South Tangerang City.

The emergence of cases of violence against children and women is often caused by factors that develop in society, for example low economic levels, education, social environment and others. Therefore, victims of such violence need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights. From the above framework, the Regional Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to suppress, prevent, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against children and women.

ON
REGIONAL REGULATION
NUMBER YEAR
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL
Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The State holds the view that all forms of violence, especially domestic violence, constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as forms of discrimination.

The State's view is based on Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, along with its amendments. Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under his/her control, and shall have the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not do something which is a basic right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to obtain facilities and special treatment to obtain the same opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice".

Current developments show that acts of physical, psychological, sexual violence, and domestic neglect in reality occur so that adequate legal instruments are needed to eliminate violence, especially domestic violence. Legal reform that sides with vulnerable or subordinated groups, especially women and children, becomes very necessary in connection with the many cases of violence, especially domestic violence, this also occurs in South Tangerang City, in 2010 violence cases reported to the Tangerang Police totaled 143 cases, at the South Jakarta Metro Police 56 cases were recorded, Tigaraksa Police - 19 - Tangerang Regency 23 cases and in 2011 70 cases were recorded at the South Jakarta Metro Police and 28 cases at the Tigaraksa Police Tangerang Regency, this does not yet reflect the actual conditions in society, because cases of violence especially those occurring within the household are still considered disgraceful in the view of society and also the courage of the community to report incidents still needs to be increased, therefore a regional regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence needs to be possessed by South Tangerang City.

The emergence of cases of violence against children and women is often caused by factors that develop in society, for example low economic levels, education, social environment and others. Therefore, victims of such violence need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights. From the above framework, the Regional Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to suppress, prevent, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against children and women.

In conducting guidance, development and protection of women and children, the role of society is needed, whether through women and children protection institutions, religious institutions, non-governmental organizations, community organizations, social organizations, business world, mass media, or educational institutions.

This Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children from violence is closely related to several other laws and regulations already in force, among others, Law Number 1 of 1946 concerning the Criminal Code and its Amendments, Law Number 8 of 1981 concerning the Criminal Procedure Code, Law Number 1 of 1974 concerning Marriage, Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human - 20 - Rights and most importantly Law number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence and Law number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

This Regional Regulation, in addition to regulating matters of prevention and protection as well as recovery for victims of violence, also regulates matters of obligations for law enforcement officers, health workers, social workers, volunteer companions, or spiritual counselors to protect victims so that they are more sensitive and responsive. To carry out violence prevention, Agencies or Offices that have duties and responsibilities related to the field of women's empowerment and child protection implement preventive actions, among others, organizing communication, information, and education about violence prevention, protection of women and children.

Based on these considerations, it is time to establish a Regional Regulation in South Tangerang City concerning the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, especially Domestic Violence, which is regulated comprehensively, clearly, and firmly to protect and side with victims, as well as simultaneously provide education and awareness to the community and officials that all acts of violence constitute crimes against human dignity.

SOURCES OF FUNDS AND REPORTING
Article 16
(1) The source of funds for the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence carried out by the regional apparatus of South Tangerang City shall be from the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of South Tangerang City.
(2) The source of funds as referred to in paragraph (1), may also come from other legal and non-binding sources.
(3) The source of funds for implementation from other legal sources as referred to in paragraph (2), shall be subject to supervision in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
(4) PPT is obligated to report the implementation of protection activities for women and children victims of violence periodically to the Mayor in accordance with applicable regulations.

Article 17
Paragraph (1) What is meant by administrative sanctions is that the institution or body that implements protection services for women and children is no longer established and or recognized by the Regional Government.
Paragraph (2) Criminal sanctions for perpetrators of violence are regulated by Law number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence article 44 through article 50; Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection Article 77 through article 90, and Law Number 1 of 1946 concerning the Criminal Code and its Amendments, Law Number 8 of 1981 concerning the Criminal Procedure Code Paragraph (3) Sufficiently clear.

Article 5
Letter a What is meant by health services are efforts that include promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects.
Letter b What is meant by receiving psychological assistance is assistance provided by a psychologist to victims who suffer from trauma/other mental problems to restore the victim's mental condition. Meanwhile, legal assistance is an aid effort provided by a person and/legal aid institution to the victim at every level of examination and throughout the legal process.
Letter c What is meant by counseling is the provision of assistance by an expert or a person who is trained in such a way that the victim's psychological understanding and ability increases in solving the problems faced.
Letter d what is meant by spiritual guidance is counseling provided by a clergyman.
Letter e What is meant by resocialization is that the victim can live life again in society including in the restoration of their good name.
Letter f What is meant by empowerment is Empowerment means making something become empowered or have power or have strength.

VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE.
CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this regional regulation, what is meant by:
1. Regional Government is the Mayor, and regional apparatus as elements of the organizer of the Regional Government of South Tangerang City.
- 8 -
2. Mayor is the Mayor of South Tangerang.
3. Implementation is the form of execution of protection for women and children victims of violence.
4. Woman is a person who has female genitalia, can experience menstruation, pregnancy, childbirth, breastfeeding and includes a person who has obtained legal status as a Woman.
5. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including those in the womb.
6. Violence is any act that results in or can result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim.
7. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
8. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death.
9. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.
10. Economic violence is any act that neglects family members in the form of not providing a proper living, care or maintenance.
11. Psychological violence is any act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person.
12. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
- 9 -
13. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutor's office, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
14. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
15. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter referred to as P2TP2A is an institution that provides services and protection for women and children especially those who have problems due to acts of violence, discrimination, human trafficking and other social problems in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psycho-social, public facility services and legal protection and assistance.
16. Community Social Institution is a Non-Governmental Organization (NGO) and or other Community Organizations.
17. Population is Citizens of South Tangerang and foreigners who enter legally and reside in the area of South Tangerang City.
18. Service is an action that must be immediately taken to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
19. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy in order to provide strengthening and recovery for victims of violence as determined in a decision of an authorized official.
20. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy and spiritual guidance for the self-strengthening of victims of violence especially victims of domestic violence to resolve the problems they face.

21. Integrated Service Center hereinafter referred to as PPT is a unified unit that carries out integrated service functions for women and children victims of violence, based in hospitals, Community Health Centers, P2TP2A and other similar institutions that are managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psycho-social and legal services.

Article 11
Paragraph (1) Sufficiently clear.

CHAPTER VI
HANDLING AND MECHANISM
Article 10
(1) The implementation of Protection for victims is carried out in an integrated manner in medical handling, legal protection, medicolegal, psychological and economic aspects, the implementation of which can be conducted through partnerships with social community institutions engaged in the protection of women and children.
(2) The implementation of protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1), must take into account religious norms as well as the rights and obligations of parents, guardians, husbands or other persons who are legally responsible for the victim.
(3) Principles of Service and Assistance:
a. Fast, safe and empathetic;
b. Guarantee of confidentiality;
c. Easily accessible;
d. No fees charged.
(4) The mechanism for handling protection as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be stipulated by Mayor Regulation.

Article 13
(1) Forms of protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence consist of medical, legal, medicolegal (forensic medicine), economic and psychological protection.
(2) The form of medical protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence as referred to in paragraph (1), consists of treatment and recovery of physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of victims carried out by medical personnel and paramedics.
- 15 - (3) The form of legal protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence as referred to in paragraph (1), consists of services and assistance to help victims undergo legal and judicial processes.
(4) The form of medicolegal protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence as referred to in paragraph (1), consists of medical services for the purpose of evidence in the legal field.
(5) The form of psychological protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence as referred to in paragraph (1), consists of assistance in order to restore the traumatic condition of victims including provision of safe houses to protect victims from various threats and intimidation for victims and providing psychological support so that victims have self-confidence, strength and independence in resolving problems.
(6) The form of economic protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence as referred to in paragraph (1), consists of services for skills and providing economic access so that victims can be independent.

Article 6
Letter a What is meant by Protection is that victims receive protection from family, police, prosecutors, courts, advocates, social institutions or other parties, either temporarily or based on a protection order from the court.
Letter b What is meant by obtaining information is the right of victims to obtain information related to prevention, complaints, medical services and protection.
Letter c What is meant by Optimal service is service that can be provided to victims in accordance with the capacity of those providing it.
Letter d What is meant by Continuous handling up to the rehabilitation stage is handling provided up to the recovery of victims in society.
Letter e What is meant by confidential handling is an effort to guarantee certainty for victims that their identity, medical treatment and legal handling will not be disseminated.
Letter f What is meant by Psychological and legal assistance is the right of victims to obtain psychological and legal assistance at every level of the examination process in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
Letter g What is meant by Guarantee of rights related to status as a family member and as a member of society.

ELUCIDATION
ON
REGIONAL REGULATION
NUMBER YEAR
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL
Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The State holds the view that all forms of violence, especially domestic violence, constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as forms of discrimination.

The State's view is based on Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, along with its amendments. Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under his/her control, and shall have the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not do something which is a basic right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to obtain facilities and special treatment to obtain the same opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice".

Current developments show that acts of physical, psychological, sexual violence, and domestic neglect in reality occur so that adequate legal instruments are needed to eliminate violence, especially domestic violence. Legal reform that sides with vulnerable or subordinated groups, especially women and children, becomes very necessary in connection with the many cases of violence, especially domestic violence, this also occurs in South Tangerang City, in 2010 violence cases reported to the Tangerang Police totaled 143 cases, at the South Jakarta Metro Police 56 cases were recorded, Tigaraksa Police - 19 - Tangerang Regency 23 cases and in 2011 70 cases were recorded at the South Jakarta Metro Police and 28 cases at the Tigaraksa Police Tangerang Regency, this does not yet reflect the actual conditions in society, because cases of violence especially those occurring within the household are still considered disgraceful in the view of society and also the courage of the community to report incidents still needs to be increased, therefore a regional regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence needs to be possessed by South Tangerang City.

The emergence of cases of violence against children and women is often caused by factors that develop in society, for example low economic levels, education, social environment and others. Therefore, victims of such violence need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights. From the above framework, the Regional Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to suppress, prevent, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against children and women.

In conducting guidance, development and protection of women and children, the role of society is needed, whether through women and children protection institutions, religious institutions, non-governmental organizations, community organizations, social organizations, business world, mass media, or educational institutions.

This Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children from violence is closely related to several other laws and regulations already in force, among others, Law Number 1 of 1946 concerning the Criminal Code and its Amendments, Law Number 8 of 1981 concerning the Criminal Procedure Code, Law Number 1 of 1974 concerning Marriage, Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human - 20 - Rights and most importantly Law number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence and Law number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

This Regional Regulation, in addition to regulating matters of prevention and protection as well as recovery for victims of violence, also regulates matters of obligations for law enforcement officers, health workers, social workers, volunteer companions, or spiritual counselors to protect victims so that they are more sensitive and responsive. To carry out violence prevention, Agencies or Offices that have duties and responsibilities related to the field of women's empowerment and child protection implement preventive actions, among others, organizing communication, information, and education about violence prevention, protection of women and children.

Based on these considerations, it is time to establish a Regional Regulation in South Tangerang City concerning the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, especially Domestic Violence, which is regulated comprehensively, clearly, and firmly to protect and side with victims, as well as simultaneously provide education and awareness to the community and officials that all acts of violence constitute crimes against human dignity.

CHAPTER VII
FORMS OF VIOLENCE AND PROTECTION
Article 11
(1) Forms of violence against Women and Children include physical, sexual, economic and psychological.
(2) Forms of physical violence are any acts that result in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and or cause death.
- 14 - (3) Forms of sexual violence are sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or specific purposes.
(4) Forms of economic violence are neglect of family members in the form of not providing a proper living, care or maintenance.
(5) Forms of psychological violence are acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering in a person.
